title: Possessors: minulla, sinulla, hänellä, meillä, teillä, heillä
focus: Finnish says who has something with a possessor form ending in -lla or -llä. This is called the adessive owner form: it names the person who has the thing.

exercises.prompt: Choose the possessor form for “I have a ball.” Frame: “___ on pallo.” Use pallo (“a ball”) and on (“have/has”).
exercises.explanation: Use minulla, the possession form of minä. The owner comes before fixed on.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Personal possessor forms: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.minulla: Use minulla, the possession form of minä. The owner comes before fixed on.
optionFeedback.sinulla: sinulla identifies you as the owner; the requested owner is I.
optionFeedback.hänellä: hänellä identifies he as the owner; the requested owner is I.
optionFeedback.meillä: meillä identifies we as the owner; the requested owner is I.
optionFeedback.teillä: teillä identifies you as the owner; the requested owner is I.
optionFeedback.heillä: heillä identifies they as the owner; the requested owner is I.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses its fixed on form with every owner, including we and they.
pallo stays in its basic singular form: one ball.
